name: NinjaTek (Fenner Precision Polymers)
summary: Flexible-filament specialist operating as a division of Fenner Precision Polymers, part of Fenner (UK), which Michelin Group acquired in May 2018. Its catalog is almost entirely TPU — NinjaFlex, Chinchilla, Cheetah, Eel and Armadillo — extruded in the US on the back of Fenner's roughly 50 years of belt and polymer extrusion experience. It also retails colorFabb-branded materials through its own shop.

oem_relationships.notes: NinjaTek's own shop (ninjatek.com/shop/) sells colorFabb-branded ASA, PA, PLA/PHA, co-polyesters and specialty fills (bronzeFill, corkFill, copperFill, glowFill, steelFill, woodFill). Products stay colorFabb-branded, so this is distribution rather than white-labelling; 'rebrands' is the closest available enum value and overstates the link. Relationship type (distribution partnership vs common ownership) is unverified. Not present in research/verified-oem-relationships.md.

product_lines.name: NinjaFlex
product_lines.notes: Shore 85A TPU - the reference product the catalog's tpu-85a entry is modelled on.

product_lines.name: NinjaFlex Edge
product_lines.notes: Shore 83A TPU with a low-tack surface texture for reliable direct-drive feeding; 2 points softer than the 85A grade.

product_lines.name: Chinchilla
product_lines.notes: NinjaTek's softest material, ~Shore 75A per third-party listings, skin-contact safe. Falls between the tpu-60a and tpu-85a grade entries, so mapped to base tpu.

product_lines.name: Armadillo
product_lines.notes: Shore 75D rigid TPU: low-warp and fracture-resistant, positioned as a PLA/ABS-stiffness alternative rather than a soft flex. Harder than the catalog's hardest graded entry (tpu-68d), so mapped to base tpu.

product_lines.name: Eel
product_lines.notes: Shore 60D TPU doped with conductive filler for static-dissipative/EMI use, 355% elongation at break. The conductive/ESD aspect is not captured by tpu-60d.

product_lines.name: colorFabb resale range
product_lines.notes: Stocked in NinjaTek's shop but formulated and branded by colorFabb, not NinjaTek: ASA, PA, PLA/PHA, co-polyesters and specialty fills (bronzeFill, copperFill, steelFill, woodFill, glowFill). Excluded from NinjaTek trade-name mappings for that reason.

additional_notes: Fenner Group's registered HQ is Hessle, England, but the NinjaTek filament operation is North American; Manheim, Pennsylvania is the commonly reported site and matches Fenner Precision Polymers' PA footprint, though it could not be confirmed from ninjatek.com in this research session. headquarters_country is therefore recorded as United States for the filament business, with UK ultimate parent ownership noted here; manufacturing_countries is United States on the strength of consistent 'Made in USA' branding. Pricing is premium for specialty TPU: MatterHackers listings for the brand ranged $48.83-$192.88 per item, with no verified $/kg. No build-plate products were found. NinjaTek pitches itself as a boutique specialty-materials brand with 'the infrastructure of a global corporation' behind it via Michelin.

provenance.conflicts: HQ is ambiguous: parent Fenner is registered in Hessle, England (confirmed) while the NinjaTek filament operation is reported as Manheim, Pennsylvania (unverified against a primary source). The colorFabb link is observed on ninjatek.com/shop/ but its nature — distribution deal vs common ownership — is unresolved, and 'rebrands' is a lossy fit for it. Exact US manufacturing site is inferred, not confirmed.
